name: SSIM图分析
description: Computes local SSIM structural similarity maps to detect region-level quality inconsistencies (Wang et al., 2004).
mechanism:
This method applies the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) framework by Wang et al. (2004) for forensic quality analysis:

1. **局部Statistics计算**: For each local window w (typically 11×11 Gaussian), three components are computed: luminance μ, contrast σ, and structure σ_xy. These capture perceptually relevant image properties following the human visual system model.

2. **SSIMComponent分解**: The SSIM index between reference and test patches decomposes as: SSIM(x,y) = l(x,y)^α · c(x,y)^β · s(x,y)^γ, where l = (2μₓμᵧ+C₁)/(μₓ²+μᵧ²+C₁), c = (2σₓσᵧ+C₂)/(σₓ²+σᵧ²+C₂), s = (σₓᵧ+C₃)/(σₓσᵧ+C₃).

3. **Self-SimilarityMapConstruction**: For forensic analysis without a reference image, local self-similarity is computed by comparing each patch against its neighboring regions. The resulting SSIM map reveals spatial consistency of image quality — genuine images show smooth, physically coherent quality variation.

4. **QualityDiscontinuity检测**: Abrupt changes in local SSIM indicate potential manipulation boundaries — where inserted or AI-generated regions meet authentic image content. These discontinuities arise from differences in compression artifacts, noise levels, or rendering quality.

5. **统计Profiling**: The distribution of local SSIM values is analyzed. Natural images exhibit characteristic SSIM distributions governed by content complexity. AI-generated images often show abnormally uniform local quality (lacking the natural variation from optics, sensor, and compression) or suspicious quality boundaries absent in untampered photographs.
parameters: 分析类型：自动统计\n分数范围：0（真实）到100（AI生成）
accuracy: 中到高 — 根据输入质量，准确率为70-85%。
source: 基于数字取证和AI内容检测的同行评审研究。
useCase: 作为多信号分析管道的一部分，用于检测AI生成的内容。
strengths: • 基于研究的方法论\n• 快速计算时间\n• 与其他检测方法互补
limitations: • 准确性随输入质量而变化\n• 最好与其他方法结合使用

references.title: Wang, Z. et al. (2004). Image Quality Assessment: From Error Visibility to Structural Similarity. IEEE TIP.
Wang, Z. & Bovik, A.C. (2009). Mean Squared Error: Love It or Leave It? IEEE Signal Processing Magazine.
